newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA DELAYS BELL COBRA HELICOPTER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA DELAYS BELL COBRA HELICOPTER.

text.p: Romania's Finance Minister said on Tuesday the government would not back in 1997 a multi- billion dollar deal to co-produce 96 Cobra attack helicopters with Bell Helicopter Textron of the United States.
"The state will not guarantee the deal with Bell Helicopters in 1997," Mircea Ciumara told Reuters.

Under the $2 billion deal, the biggest project in post- communist Romania, a venture between the local Intreprinderea Aeronautica Romana (IAR) aircraft maker and Bell was to produce 96 AH-1RO Dracula helicopters, derived from the AH-1W Supercobra used by the U.S. Marine Corps.

The move is part of the country's efforts to align its military equipment to NATO standards, with an eye to an securing eventual membership of the Alliance after being refused entry in the first wave last month.
Ciumara made no mention of a new deadline for the deal.

He made his remarks as the government headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea met an International Monetary Fund mission on a revised budget. A new budget is one of the IMF's conditions for releasing the second of five $86 million credits.

Media reports earlier in the day said the IMF had opposed demands by the government to extend by two billion dollars the ceiling of its external borrowings -- a measure which would have included the funds for the Cobra deal.
Those reports were not confirmed by government or IMF officials.
